title: List Coding Agent Slack Authors (Admin)
description: Returns distinct authors of collected Coding Agent mentions for an admin author selector. Requires the authenticated account to be a Recoup admin, using exactly one of x-api-key or Authorization Bearer. No query parameters are defined. Each authorized request runs the existing all-period Slack collector once, then deduplicates by Slack author ID, retains the first collected profile and sorts by display name using localeCompare; identical names do not merge different IDs. The result is authors in that collected data, not a complete all-time Slack directory. Existing channel access, retention, paginated history, first-page thread replies and partial-failure limits remain; partial collection can still produce an incomplete successful result. Thrown collection failures return 500. This call is not free cached metadata: a future caller must account for scan latency and quotas. The release adds no automatic caller, UI, polling, scheduled action, new Slack scope or Slack send. Production admin access, history coverage, latency and quotas were not verified by the source contract tests.

title: Admin signup report availability
description: An admin key-metadata report is available; the former signup-report URL and broader reporting outcome remain separate.
body:
`GET /api/admins/agent/signups` is not available. The new
[admin key-metadata report](/api-reference/admins/agent-key-metadata) uses
`GET /api/admins/agent-signups` (a different URL).

A Recoup admin can use the new report to inspect key-record IDs, names, creation
times and matching current `agent+…` email addresses. It never returns API-key
credentials or hashes. Its `total` counts the returned key records; several keys
can belong to one account. It does not establish where an account signed up,
how many unique agents signed up, which keys are active, or whether people use
the product. Current email associations, database visibility and server row limits
also prevent a guarantee of complete historical reporting.

## Unfinished reporting outcome

[Reconciliation #327](https://github.com/recoupable/mono/issues/327) retains the
broader reporting decision. The bounded metadata route from
[API #1095](https://github.com/recoupable/api/pull/1095) does not complete the original
[API #428](https://github.com/recoupable/api/issues/428) customer outcome or restore
the former URL. Follow the new route's period, admin-access and collection-limit
notes when using it; do not treat key-record counts as signup-origin or adoption
measurements.

title: Credit Usage Events (Admin)
description: Returns the raw `usage_events` rows for a single account over the selected period, sorted by `created_at` descending. title: Connection Ownership
description: The connector connection-ownership and authority contract: who owns a connection, who can act through it, and why roster membership never grants execute rights.
body:
## Overview

Connectors link third-party services (Google Sheets, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, and others) to Recoup so agents can act on an artist's behalf. This page defines the **ownership and authority contract** for those connections: who a connection belongs to, and who is allowed to authorize, execute through, or disconnect it.

This contract is the source of truth for connector access control. Endpoint request and response shapes are documented separately in the [Connectors API reference](/api-reference/connectors/list).

---

## Association ≠ Authority

Artists in Recoup are **canonical and shared**. The same artist can appear in many accounts' rosters and in multiple organizations. Being associated with an artist is not the same as having authority to act through that artist's connections:

- An artist appearing in an account's roster (`account_artist_ids`) grants **read and analytics access only**.
- An artist appearing in an organization's roster likewise grants **read and analytics access only** to org members.
- Neither form of association ever grants the right to authorize, execute, or disconnect a connection.

<Warning>
Roster membership never inherits connection authority. If Account A connects an artist's TikTok, Account B having that same artist on its roster does **not** let Account B post through that connection.
</Warning>

---

## Connection Scope

Connections are scoped to the **relationship between an owner and an artist**, not to the bare canonical artist:

| Connection type | Scoped to |
|-----------------|-----------|
| Personal | The `(account, artist)` pair |
| Org-shared | The `(organization, artist)` pair |

The connection is keyed on the **join row** (the specific account-to-artist or org-to-artist relationship), never on the canonical artist alone. Two accounts that both roster the same artist hold two independent connection scopes for that artist.

**Whoever establishes a connection owns it.** Ownership is set at authorization time and does not transfer through roster changes.

Because artists stay canonical and shared, **isolation lives on the connection**: sharing an artist across accounts and orgs is safe precisely because each connection is confined to the relationship that created it.

---

## Authority Matrix

| Capability | Who has it |
|------------|-----------|
| Read / analytics on an artist | Any account or org member with the artist in their roster |
| Authorize a new connection | The account (or org member, for org-shared) establishing the connection, who then owns it |
| Execute actions through a connection | The owning account only; for org-shared connections, members of the owning org |
| Disconnect a connection | The owning account only; for org-shared connections, members of the owning org |
| Admin override | Recoup staff only (admins of the Recoup internal organization) |

<Note>
The admin override exists for support and abuse response. No customer account or organization, regardless of roster or org membership, can override another owner's connection.
</Note>

---

## Relationship to the Current API Reference

The [Connectors endpoint reference](/api-reference/connectors/list) currently describes connections as scoped to the authenticated account alone. That reflects behavior that shipped before this contract; the API is being re-keyed to the per-`(account, artist)` / per-`(organization, artist)` model defined here. Where the two disagree, **this page is the authority contract**. Endpoint docs will be updated as the re-keyed API ships.

Endpoint request and response shapes for the re-keyed model are deliberately not documented here yet.

title: Check an application proposal
description: Validate proposed app addresses in your workspace without registering or activating an application.
body:
<Warning>
  Pending coordinated release. This checks a proposal; it does not register an
  app or make its origins trusted. Discover tool availability in your connected
  host before use.
</Warning>

Before connecting an external app, check its proposed name, environment, origins
and return URLs. A successful result means those values passed validation for
the selected workspace. It does not prove domain ownership.

## What happens

The preflight runs after normal Recoup authentication. First-time sign-in can
perform normal account provisioning and send its welcome email. After that,
this validator does not persist an application or issue application credentials.
It does not edit provider callbacks, create fan identities or sessions, allocate
capacity, or authorize purchases and spending.

`workspace_id` and `billing_owner_id` come from the authenticated account or an
organization it can access. They describe the proposed owner only. Supplying
`organization_id` does not grant workspace access. Do not submit account or
billing ownership overrides, secrets or tokens in the proposal.

The result is flat and includes `status: "validated"`, `persisted: false` and
`origins_verified: false`. It contains no application ID or token to install.

## Addresses and environments

- Choose `development` or `production` explicitly for each proposal.
- Use exact canonical origins such as `https://music.example`, without a trailing
  slash, wildcard, path, credentials, query or fragment. Different hosts and
  ports are different origins.
- HTTPS is required. Development also accepts HTTP on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`
  and `[::1]`; these loopback hosts are rejected in production.
- A return URL must be an exact canonical URL on one of the proposed origins,
  without credentials or fragments. For a bare host use its canonical trailing
  slash, such as `https://music.example/`. Query strings are retained literally.
- Each list takes 1–32 distinct addresses, each at most 2048 characters. The name
  is trimmed and must then contain 1–120 characters. These are input limits,
  not subscription or usage allowances.

Matching a return URL to a caller-proposed origin does not establish that the
caller owns either address. No DNS check, URL fetch or domain proof is performed.

## Standard MCP

On a standard API-key MCP connection that exposes `validate_application_registration`,
use the same proposal fields as HTTP. Account identity comes from the connection;
do not add `account_id` or extract a host-managed OAuth token.

```json
{
  "name": "Release companion",
  "environment": "production",
  "allowed_origins": ["https://music.example"],
  "return_urls": ["https://music.example/listen?connected=spotify"]
}
```

Delegated OAuth excludes this tool, including connections with `mcp:tools`.
HTTP and standard MCP share proposal validation; their transport-specific error
envelopes differ. HTTP authentication errors can use `error` or `message`, while
handled preflight errors use `status: "error"` and `error`. MCP failures are tool
errors or SDK input-validation errors. None confirms registration or activation.

See [authentication](/authentication) and [MCP connection guidance](/mcp).
Application persistence, origin proof/reverification, provider configuration,
fan bootstrap, suspension and quota policy require their own completed contracts.

title: Sites
description: Create, generate, and publish fan experiences through the API or MCP.
body:
Sites uses the same backend operations from the web app, HTTP API, and MCP. A new site is a **private draft**. Generation never publishes it automatically.

## Authentication

Private HTTP endpoints accept exactly one of `x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY` or `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
MCP uses the existing authenticated `https://api.recoupable.dev/mcp` connection.

The caller is derived from authentication. Do not send an `account_id`. An optional `organizationId` selects a workspace the caller can access. Omit it for the authenticated account's workspace.

## Endpoints and tools

| HTTP | MCP tool | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sites` | `list_sites` | `{ sites: [...] }` |
| `POST /api/sites` | `create_site` | `{ site: ... }`, HTTP 201 |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}` | `get_site` | `{ site: ... }` |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `concepts` | `propose_site_concepts` | Short pitches or missing context |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `generate` | `generate_site` | Generate from an optional customer-selected pitch; otherwise select a concept |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `generation` | `get_site_generation` | Status for the specified generation token |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `publish` | `publish_site` | Publish the saved draft or the playable build selected by `generationToken` |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `unpublish` | `unpublish_site` | Public snapshot removed, draft retained |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `delete` | `delete_site` | `{ "deleted": true, "id": "..." }` |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/signups` | `get_site_signups` | `{ signups: [{ email, created_at }] }`, up to 10,000 |
| `POST /api/sites/assets` | `upload_site_asset` | `{ asset: { url, name, type } }` |

Listing accepts optional `organizationId` and `artistId` query parameters. All private reads and writes verify workspace access. Signup emails are never part of the public response.

## Create and generate

Create a draft with a Spotify track, album, or playlist URL. Recoup retrieves its title and artwork. The brief is optional; without it, Recoup uses the available song and artist context to propose activities. Alternatively, supply both a name and a brief without a release URL.

```bash
curl https://api.recoupable.dev/api/sites \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"releaseUrl":"https://open.spotify.com/track/TRACK_ID","brief":"Build a maze game"}'
```

Optional creation fields: `name` (120 characters), `brief` (6,000), `organizationId`, `artistId`, and `assets` (up to eight workspace-owned assets returned by the upload endpoint). An artist must be accessible to the caller and belong to the selected organization when one is used.

Read `site.id` and `site.revision`, then start automatic generation:

```json
{"action":"generate","revision":0}
```

For Spotify tracks, the background workflow saves metadata, acquires and verifies full audio, saves Music Flamingo lyrics and musical analysis, collects artwork observations and public artist research, compiles a saved brief, selects a concept, and builds and reviews the site. No separate collector calls are required. Audio acquisition requires a Spotify preview for waveform verification and stops if no matching full recording is found. Completed accepted context is reused.

To choose a concept yourself before generation, optionally request pitches:

```json
{"action":"concepts","revision":0}
```

Send this to `PATCH /api/sites/{id}`, or call MCP `propose_site_concepts` with `id` and `revision`. Optional `instruction` and `contextBriefId` apply to pitching too. This can use credits for context collection and a pitch call, but does not create images, site code or change the draft.

The response is `{ concepts: { status, candidates, reason }, revision }`. Status is `ready`, `needs-context`, or `no-good-concept`. Metadata and cover details alone return `needs-context`; provide usable song analysis or sourced artist context rather than forcing an activity out of the artwork.

In the explicit-selection flow, show the short pitches to the customer and wait for their choice. Each candidate contains `name`, `activity`, `fanMotivation`, `songOrArtistConnection`, and `friendHook`. Pass the selected object unchanged as `approvedConcept`:

```json
{
  "action": "generate",
  "revision": 0,
  "approvedConcept": {
    "name": "CUSTOMER_SELECTED_NAME",
    "activity": "SELECTED_ACTIVITY",
    "fanMotivation": "SELECTED_MOTIVATION",
    "songOrArtistConnection": "SELECTED_CONNECTION",
    "friendHook": "SELECTED_HOOK"
  }
}
```

MCP `generate_site` accepts the same fields plus `id`, without `action`. A customer-authored concept is also accepted. The optional `approvedConcept` preserves a caller-selected activity. When omitted, the engine selects from its proposed concepts after collecting context.

Generation defaults to background execution and returns a generation token; poll `get_site_generation` (HTTP action `generation`) for the result. Set `background: false` only for a synchronous client that supports a long timeout. If review rejects the concept, the draft is marked `needs-review`; the system does not silently substitute a new activity. Asset and implementation repairs retain their bounded pass.

Generation failures identify the stopped stage and leave the saved draft unchanged. A `409` means another edit changed the revision; read the site again before retrying.

### Poll background generation

Send this JSON body to `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` using the token returned by the
generation request. MCP `get_site_generation` takes `id` and `token`, without `action`.
Polling uses `token`; publishing and cancellation use `generationToken`.

```json
{"action":"generation","token":"TOKEN_FROM_GENERATION"}
```

The token is bound to its site and caller and expires. Invalid, expired or
mismatched tokens return 404 during token verification; a missing or empty token
is invalid input (400). A running job is not proof that a
playable build or a published page exists; read the returned status and progress.

## Generate from saved Context Engine evidence

Save a single-song `creative_direction` brief using the Context Engine `save_brief` action, then pass its snapshot ID when requesting pitches:

```json
{
  "action": "concepts",
  "revision": 0,
  "contextBriefId": "SAVED_BRIEF_UUID"
}
```

Pass the same `contextBriefId` with the selected `approvedConcept` to generation. It is available on both MCP `propose_site_concepts` and `generate_site`. Without a saved brief, track generation automatically collects and saves context, reusing compatible accepted module results. The brief must belong to the site's workspace and match its Spotify track. Sites rejects unavailable or superseded snapshots before generation. Revisions reuse the draft's selected brief unless a new ID is supplied.

This path reuses accepted song summaries, artwork observations, public artist research and release/artist metadata instead of collecting them again. The creative director and generator receive attribution, coverage and missing-topic information. Supported evidence includes public Spotify metadata/artwork, YouTube-attributed audio analysis and saved public-search research. Private uploads, customer assertions and raw lyrics are excluded. Matching saved machine transcripts inform paraphrased themes but are not forwarded to the site. Partial evidence stays partial.

Generation still uses credits for creative direction, assets, implementation and review. It saves a private draft, never publishes automatically. Snapshot availability is checked again before saving and publishing. Later source withdrawal does not automatically retract an already published site. Internal evidence and source identifiers are excluded from the public site response.

## Publish

After reviewing the intended draft or preview, publish through the same PATCH
endpoint or MCP `publish_site`, using the site's current saved revision.

Publishing automatically prepares Spotify fan connection for an active paid workspace. The standard agreement uses the attributed artist's name; the customer does not need a separate setup step. Missing artist attribution or unavailable Spotify configuration stops paid publication with an actionable error. Publication requires an eligible paid workspace. The gate checks the site's owning workspace for an active subscription with a positive-priced item; a trial or Pro entitlement alone does not establish eligibility. Unpaid publication returns HTTP 402 before publishing. Successful paid setup reports `fanConnection: "enabled"`.

For a custom hosted destination, HTTP callers may include `returnUrl` (an HTTPS URL without credentials or fragment) in the publish body. Otherwise an existing connection destination is preserved, or the configured Sites public origin is used. The Recoup editor supplies its actual published URL. The authenticated fan-connection API remains available for external integrations.

The public page is `https://chat.recoupable.dev/s/{id}`.

### Publish the saved draft

Use the current revision from the saved site (3 in this example):

```json
{"action":"publish","revision":3}
```

Omitting `generationToken` selects the saved draft, even when a background job has
a newer preview. MCP `publish_site` takes `id` and `revision`, without `action`.

### Publish a working preview

To publish a specific working preview from a background generation, pass its
token as `generationToken` and the site's current saved revision:

```json
{"action":"publish","revision":3,"generationToken":"TOKEN_FROM_GENERATION"}
```

MCP `publish_site` uses the same fields plus `id`, without `action`. The token must
match the site and caller. The selected build must contain a completed playable
build step for the current site/workspace/revision; the whole generation job need
not already be completed. A preview that is not ready returns 400, a stale build
returns 409, and invalid or expired token access returns 404. A temporary saved-build
failure may return 503. Without `generationToken`, publication uses the saved draft;
it does not automatically select the newest background preview.

### Upgrade required

An ineligible workspace receives HTTP 402 with an error body, for example:

```json
{"error":"An active paid Recoup subscription is required to publish a site. Subscribe in this site’s workspace, then publish again."}
```

Subscribe in the site's owning workspace before retrying the intended publish.
This response does not publish the site or create a checkout session.

### Unpublish

Send `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` with the current revision to remove the public
snapshot while retaining the draft. MCP `unpublish_site` takes `id` and `revision`.

```json
{"action":"unpublish","revision":3}
```

Agents should publish, unpublish or delete only when explicitly instructed.

## Delete and cancel generation

Delete only when explicitly instructed. Send `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` with `action: "delete"` and the current `revision` in its JSON request body (Content-Type: application/json). Include `generationToken` when cancelling a known in-progress generation. The token must belong to this site and caller; cancellation is attempted before deletion. Omitting it does not request cancellation of every running job.

For example, use the current saved revision and the token returned by a known generation:

```json
{"action":"delete","revision":3,"generationToken":"TOKEN_FROM_GENERATION"}
```

Omit generationToken when no known generation needs cancellation.

Deletion checks workspace access and revision, then returns `{ "deleted": true, "id": "..." }`. A stale revision returns 409; reload before retrying. Unpublish with `action: "unpublish"` when the draft should remain available.

## Uploads

HTTP uploads are multipart forms with a `file` field and optional `organizationId` query parameter. Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, MP3, and WAV, up to 4 MB per file. Images are re-encoded to WebP. Audio is checked for its file signature.

MCP's `upload_site_asset` accepts `name`, `contentType`, `base64` file bytes, and optional `organizationId`. It uses the same validation and storage path as HTTP.

## Public endpoints

- `GET /api/sites/public/{id}` returns `{ snapshot: ... }` for a published site only. Drafts, account identifiers, and signup data are excluded.
- `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/signup` accepts `{"email":"fan@example.com","consent":"yes"}`. An optional `website` honeypot must be empty. Duplicate submissions succeed without disclosing list membership. Unpublished sites reject signups.

Public pages and the browser music player render in the chat app. The API provides
snapshots, generation, uploads, signup persistence and the fan-connection integration
routes listed below.

## Route coverage

The lifecycle and public snapshot/signup operations above are documented here in
prose; they are not a complete Sites OpenAPI specification. The following existing
routes are accounted for as integration surfaces, outside the copyable lifecycle
examples. Listing them does not establish live authorization or add an MCP tool.

### Authenticated integration routes

| HTTP | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/fan-connection` | Read fan-connection configuration |
| `PUT /api/sites/{id}/fan-connection` | Configure the fan connection through the authenticated integration |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/fans` | Fan reporting |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/activity` | Activity reporting |

### Browser integration routes

| HTTP | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sites/apple/config` | Browser music configuration |
| `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/activity` | Published-site activity collection |
| `GET /api/sites/public/{id}/spotify` | Show the fan-connection acceptance page |
| `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/spotify` | Begin Spotify authorization after acceptance |

These browser flows are not replacements for a private lifecycle request or proof
of a completed fan connection. Email signup and Spotify connection are distinct.

### Provider callback

`GET /api/sites/spotify/callback` completes the provider redirect flow. It is
intentionally excluded from agent lifecycle examples; do not invoke it as a
standalone operation. OPTIONS preflight handlers are also excluded from the
operation tables because they serve browser CORS negotiation.

## Errors

- `402`: publication requires an eligible paid workspace.

`400` invalid input; `401` missing/invalid authentication; `403` workspace or artist access denied; `404` missing/unpublished site; `409` stale revision; `422` Spotify metadata unavailable; `503` temporary operation failure.

title: Connect Spotify fans to a site
description: Configure paid fan connection from an artist agent and retrieve fans attributed to its site.
body:
Release dependency: these routes require the site fan connection API release and its database migration. The skill alone does not enable them. Base URL: `https://api.recoupable.dev`.

Private calls use `x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY` (or the platform's existing bearer authentication). Customer credentials stay with the agent/server. Public connection entry and callback use browser-bound OAuth state, not the customer API key.

## Customer and site

- `GET /api/accounts/id`: verify the current credential.
- `POST /api/agents/signup` with `{ "email": "customer@example.com" }`: request email verification.
- `POST /api/agents/verify` with `{ "email": "customer@example.com", "code": "123456" }`: receive `api_key`; never echo it.
- `GET /api/artists`: inspect the caller's roster and choose the artist's account ID.
- `GET /api/sites`: inspect existing site records.
- `POST /api/sites` with `{ "name": "Release experience", "artistId": "ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID", "releaseUrl": "https://open.spotify.com/track/TRACK_ID" }`: register a site. Add `organizationId` only for a selected authorized workspace. Read the returned `site.id`. Omit owner/account ID fields; ownership comes from authentication.

## Configure

`GET /api/sites/{siteId}/fan-connection` returns:

```json
{
  "siteId": "SITE_UUID",
  "ownerId": "WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT_UUID",
  "artistId": "ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID",
  "config": null,
  "connectUrl": null
}
```

Existing `config` contains `site_id`, `return_url`, `marketing_text`, `enabled` and `revision`. Update with `PUT /api/sites/{siteId}/fan-connection`:

```json
{
  "returnUrl": "https://artist.example/release",
  "marketingText": "I agree to receive release announcements and offers by email from Example Artist.",
  "enabled": true,
  "revision": 0
}
```

Use the real artist's approved text, not the example unchanged. Return URL must be HTTPS, at most 2048 characters, without credentials or fragments. Text length is 20–1000 characters. Pass the last read revision, or 0 for initial configuration. The response has the same envelope with persisted config and the public `connectUrl`; always use that returned URL.

- 400: invalid input or missing artist attribution.
- 401/403: reconnect the customer or select an authorized workspace.
- 402: no eligible paid subscription for the site's owning account.
- 404: missing site or API not deployed; inspect the actual response.
- 409: another configuration update won; reload and reconcile before retry.
- 503: provider, billing or storage unavailable; surface the dependency.

Spotify fan connection is included in an active paid Recoup subscription owned by the site's workspace. No separate add-on is required. Existing `POST /api/subscriptions/sessions` accepts `{plan: "starter" | "pro", successUrl, cancelUrl?}` and returns the customer checkout URL. Let the customer complete payment; then retry activation. Fans do not buy this feature.

## Public fan journey

`GET /api/sites/public/{siteId}/spotify` displays the site's agreement. Its own form POST binds acceptance to that browser and configuration revision, then redirects to Spotify PKCE authorization. Do not handcraft this POST or bypass the page. Spotify returns to Recoup's `/api/sites/spotify/callback`; Recoup then returns to the configured site URL with `recoup_spotify=connected`, `cancelled` or `failed`.

Only a successful provider exchange with `user-read-email` and `user-read-private` creates records. Actual granted scopes and the exact accepted marketing text are retained separately from the successful connection. Email may be absent. No tokens or profile details are passed to the public site.

## Read fans

`GET /api/sites/{siteId}/fans?offset=0&limit=50` (private):

```json
{
  "fans": [],
  "total": 0,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 50
}
```

Each fan has `id`, `site_id`, `spotify_id`, `display_name`, `email`, first/last connection timestamps and nested `site_fan_connections` with `site_fan_permissions` and `site_fan_marketing_consents`. Paginate up to 100 fans per page. Records are private to authorized workspace members. Read access remains available after paid eligibility expires. Repeated connection updates the existing fan for that site and adds a connection history entry. The site's owner and artist supply attribution. These records are separate from email-only signups and other artist audience data.

Starter Checkout can return HTTP 400 `starter_unavailable` when its price is not
configured. Explain the unavailable option and use a configured plan; do not retry
it as a transient provider failure.

## Recoup operator setup

Operators must apply `20260928010000_site_fan_connections.sql`, configure `SITES_SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, register an HTTPS callback ending `/api/sites/spotify/callback`, set `SITES_FAN_SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI`. This is Recoup service configuration, not work to impose on each artist. The existing browser playback callback remains separate.

## Activity reporting

`GET /api/sites/{siteId}/activity` returns 30-day counts for visits, starts, completions, replays and shares to authorized workspace members. `POST /api/sites/public/{siteId}/activity` accepts `{id: EVENT_UUID, visitId: VISIT_UUID, event: "visit" | "start" | "complete" | "replay" | "share"}`. Reuse the event UUID when retrying. Use a site-scoped visit ID. Never send emails, profile data or arbitrary page contents to this endpoint. These are browser-reported interactions, not verified Spotify listening or a named fan activity history.

Recoup-hosted generated sites use the trusted host bridge: `window.recoup.track(event)` reports approved events; `window.recoup.join()` reveals the trusted signup controls. External sites should implement the equivalent fixed-event transport and keep account credentials on the server.

## Playback for Premium and Free listeners

The hosted player reads the connected Spotify profile's `product` field. Premium listeners use the Spotify Web Playback SDK. Free (`free` or `open`) listeners use the site's saved, verified recording through the same play/pause, seek and volume controls. If the profile cannot be read, its subscription remains unknown; available artist audio keeps playback usable. The player also handles a Spotify SDK account rejection by switching to the recording.

`GET /api/sites/public/{siteId}` includes `playbackAudioUrl`, a fresh signed audio URL valid for one hour, or `null` when no matching verified recording is available. It is resolved from the published site's workspace-owned context request and matching Spotify track; private research and analysis are excluded. Fetch a fresh public response when reloading rather than storing this URL permanently. Publish only audio you have permission to serve to fans.

File playback is not a Spotify stream. Spotify playback subscription, Recoup's paid fan-connection entitlement, and fan capture are separate concerns. A missing audio file must show an honest unavailable state while keeping the game playable.

title: One player for every release
description: Create a listening page or embed Spotify and Apple Music playback on your artist website.
body:
Create a player for a song, album or Spotify playlist. Share its listening page or embed it on your website. Recoup handles music-service sign-in, supported browser playback and fan activity reporting.

## Create and publish

Use the [Recoup API](/api-reference/players/create) or the `create_release_player` MCP tool. Choose an artist you can access, name the player, and provide a `spotifyUrl`, an `appleUrl`, or both. Use `organizationId` to create it in your organization workspace.

For website embeds, add the exact website origins to `allowedOrigins`. An origin includes the scheme, hostname and any non-default port, such as `https://artist.example:8443`. Embed origins must use HTTPS. Include both the www and non-www origins if fans can visit either. You can omit this field when sharing only the hosted listening page.

Example create request:

```json
{
  "artistId": "ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID",
  "organizationId": "ORGANIZATION_UUID",
  "name": "Release title",
  "spotifyUrl": "https://open.spotify.com/album/ALBUM_ID",
  "appleUrl": "https://music.apple.com/us/album/release/APPLE_ID",
  "allowedOrigins": ["https://artist.example", "https://www.artist.example"]
}
```

New players start unpublished. Review the music links, then publish with `update_release_player`, passing `id`, the current `revision`, and `enabled: true`. Publishing requires an active paid Recoup workspace.

Use the same tool to change the music links, title, artwork or approved website origins. Pass the current revision returned by Recoup with each update. The player stays assigned to its original artist and workspace. Updating it ends existing player sessions, so fans may need to reconnect.

See [update a release player](/api-reference/players/update) for the REST request and fields.

## Share a listening page

Use the returned `listenUrl` as your bio or campaign link. No custom website is needed. Fans choose from the music services configured for that player.

To track campaign traffic, add `source`, `medium`, `campaign`, and `content` query parameters. The listening page also accepts `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, and `utm_content`. Use campaign labels, such as `instagram` and `release`; keep personal information out of links.

## Embed on your website

Use the returned `spotifyEmbedUrl` or `appleEmbedUrl` for each configured service. The `parent` parameter must match an approved website origin.

```html
<iframe
  src="https://app.recoupable.dev/listen/PLAYER_UUID/spotify?parent=https%3A%2F%2Fartist.example&source=instagram&campaign=release"
  title="Recoup music player"
  allow="autoplay; encrypted-media"
></iframe>
```

Keep music-service sign-in inside the Recoup player. Your website does not need Spotify or Apple credentials. Include a direct music-service link as a fallback when browser playback is unavailable.

For Spotify Free handoffs, the embed sends a `recoup:open-dsp` message with `provider: "spotify"`. Your website must verify that the message comes from the Recoup player origin and that iframe's window, then open the Spotify destination configured for the player. Do not use a destination URL supplied by a message.

## What fans can play

Spotify Premium fans can stream through the browser player after connecting. Spotify playlist players show a selectable song list and highlight the current song. Selecting a song starts playback at its position in the playlist. Unavailable entries cannot be selected. If the list fails to load, fans can retry or open the playlist in Spotify.

Spotify Free fans are sent to the configured song, album or playlist in Spotify after connecting. Spotify controls whether that opens in its app or website and which playback options the fan has. If Recoup cannot confirm the account's subscription, it does not assume the account is Free.

Apple Music playback uses the fan's Apple Music authorization and subscription. Apple sessions do not capture email or create an identified fan contact in Recoup.

## Optional uploaded audio for Spotify Free fans

You can choose to let Spotify Free fans play an uploaded audio file in Recoup instead of sending them to Spotify. Set `freePlayback: "audio"` and provide `audioUrl`. This setting belongs to the player owner; fans cannot change it. Premium fans continue to stream from Spotify.

Upload an MP3 or WAV through `POST /api/sites/assets` in the same workspace, then use the returned `asset.url`. The current upload limit is 4 MB. Audio mode requires a Spotify destination as a fallback.

MCP arguments for `update_release_player`:

```json
{
  "id": "PLAYER_UUID",
  "revision": 1,
  "freePlayback": "audio",
  "audioUrl": "WORKSPACE_UPLOADED_ASSET_URL"
}
```

For REST, send `PATCH /api/players/PLAYER_UUID` with the same body except `id`; the player ID belongs in the URL.

Audio mode plays one uploaded file per player. It does not support an uploaded playlist or generate Spotify streams. Uploaded-file playback is excluded from the player's music-service playback reports; fan connections are still recorded. If the file is missing, fans are sent to Spotify. If it fails to load, the player offers an Open in Spotify link.

To restore the Spotify handoff, set `freePlayback: "spotify"`. You can also clear `audioUrl` by setting it to `null`.

## Fan contacts belong to your workspace

Spotify sign-in captures the profile information and email that Spotify makes available. A returning Spotify account reuses its contact in the same workspace.

If that fan connects to another artist in your workspace, Recoup adds an artist relationship to the same contact. If they connect in another organization, that organization gets a separate contact. Your contact and listening history stay in your workspace. Matching names or email addresses alone do not merge fans.

- Use `get_workspace_player_fans` or [read workspace player fans](/api-reference/players/workspace-fans) to list contacts and their artist relationships.
- Use `get_release_player_fans` or [read artist player fans](/api-reference/players/fans) to list fan relationships across that artist's players in the workspace.

`contact_id` identifies the workspace contact. Each artist relationship has its own `id`; activity records refer to that relationship as `fan_id`.

Spotify sign-in does **not** grant email marketing consent. Use a separate, optional signup before sending marketing emails. Apple Music sessions remain anonymous and are not linked to Spotify contacts.

## Measure listening activity

Use `get_release_player_activity` or [read listening activity](/api-reference/players/activity) for 30-day campaign totals and individual track, play, pause and skip events.

These reports describe activity observed while the Recoup player is open. Playback after a fan leaves for Spotify or Apple Music is outside these reports. Player events and reported listening time are **not confirmed music-service stream counts** and do not prove that a campaign caused additional streams. Compare them with catalog stream measurements to evaluate campaign performance.

## Check your fan journey

Before promoting the link, test it on the phones and social browsers your fans use. Confirm that sign-in works, the correct music opens, playlist songs can be selected, and the Spotify Free fallback works. Then check fan and activity reports in the intended workspace.

title: Record reported listening
description: Internal trusted Recoup player transport. Requires its Origin plus signed flow; browser-facing same-origin app proxy forwards to API. Provider and fan attribution come from the stored session. Event UUID makes retries idempotent, listenedMs is capped at 30 seconds and checked against elapsed server time. Recording failures do not stop music.

title: Exchange player Spotify authorization
description: Internal trusted Recoup player endpoint, not an external website integration. Requires a fresh Spotify listening session, PKCE code/verifier, API-configured OAuth app and required scopes. Captures Spotify-confirmed available profile/email for the registered artist/workspace. Returns provider credentials only to the trusted Recoup browser, plus player_session_id and fanCapture; no email/fan ID in the response. Tokens are not persisted in fan tables. A failed capture reports fanCapture=false while valid playback credentials remain usable. Authorization is not email marketing consent.
